findings.evidence: `rg`/line hits: code lines 218 and 221 require order `1`; `ConditionB` lines 267-272 only adds `SectorCompatible`; roadmap `Suggested.lean` lines 102-106 and README lines 182-185 state A′ includes a prescribed pole order.
findings.fix: Make A′ order-aware, e.g. by passing `f`/pole orders or replacing `S : Finset ℂ` with ordered singularity data, and require flatness of the required pole order at every crossing; otherwise do not export this as the HW A′ condition consumed by the general residue theorem.
findings.issue: `ConditionAprime` hard-codes `FlatOfOrder ... 1` for interior crossings and `FlatOfOrderBasepoint ... 1` at the basepoint, so a higher-order on-curve pole can satisfy A′ with only first-order flatness.

findings.evidence: Code lines 189-190 and 199-200 use `‖γ t - (γ t₀ + (t - t₀) • t_plus)‖` and endpoint analogues; the doc at lines 183-186 acknowledges the predicate is stricter than HW Def. 3.2 for `n ≥ 2`.
findings.fix: Define higher-order flatness using distance to the one-sided tangent line/projection, or restrict/rename this predicate so it is not the general HW flatness notion used for higher-order A′.
findings.issue: `FlatOfOrder`/`FlatOfOrderBasepoint` measure error from the parametrized affine point `γ t₀ + (t - t₀) • v`, not distance to the tangent line/projection required by HW flatness for order `n`; for `n ≥ 2` this rejects curves that are geometrically flat along the tangent line with nonlinear speed.

summary: ConditionAprime still implements only first-order transversality while the roadmap/HW condition requires flatness matched to prescribed pole order; the general flatness predicate also does not formalize HW's tangent-line definition for higher orders.
